name: Pallet
summary: Pallet builds software for transportation and warehouse operations, giving freight businesses a more automated operating system for dispatch, billing, and back-office workflows.
overview: Pallet builds software for transportation and warehouse operators. Its platform targets the operational work behind freight movement, including dispatch, billing, and back-office workflows.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: General Catalyst led the $27 million Series B; the valuation was not disclosed.

facts.label: Public status
facts.note: No confirmed public offering is reflected in this profile.

bull_case: Freight operators still manage complex, fragmented workflows. A product that consolidates those systems can become deeply embedded in customers' operations.
bear_case: Logistics software competes for budgets with incumbent systems and in-house processes, while end-market freight volumes can be cyclical.
directory_notes: Watch for customer adoption and operating-scale disclosures.

intelligence.description: Pallet provides transportation and warehouse software for freight operators.

metrics.label: Latest valuation
metrics.note: Valuation was not announced with the May 2025 Series B

company: Pallet sells software intended to help transportation and warehouse operators run day-to-day workflows. Its focus is the operational layer of freight, where dispatch, billing, and workflow coordination are often handled across fragmented tools.
In May 2025, Pallet raised a $27 million Series B led by General Catalyst. The company did not disclose a valuation with that financing.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Pallet is a useful read-through on whether vertical software can modernize a large, operationally complex freight market. Its progress matters to investors watching workflow automation beyond the most crowded enterprise software categories.

changed.text: Pallet completed a $27 million Series B led by General Catalyst.

takeaways: Pallet addresses operational software needs in transportation and warehousing.
Its May 2025 Series B was led by General Catalyst.
The financing did not include a disclosed valuation.
Customer adoption and retention are the principal indicators to watch.
